title: Skills and ACD
summary: How Genesys Cloud matches a skill request to an agent, from the ACD idea through filters, rings, and direct routing.

lessons.title: ACD is the match, and skills are one way to make it
lessons.summary: Wikipedia describes an ACD as a distributor. Genesys Cloud puts that job on the queue’s routing method.
paras: The Wikipedia article describes an automatic call distributor as a system that answers and distributes incoming calls, and it describes skills-based routing as routing by an operator’s knowledge. Genesys Cloud’s evaluation article is more specific: ACD uses the queue’s routing method to match interactions and agents. When the method is skills-based, the evaluation method decides how a skill request is processed. A customer can request skills from the IVR.

The queue settings article lists five routing methods: standard, predictive, bullseye, preferred agent, and conditional group. The advanced routing overview describes those and also describes direct routing, which sends the interaction to a dedicated person instead of the next available agent. Direct routing is not a sixth choice in that five-method list. The ACD track in this lab drills the five methods. This chapter adds the filter, the ring-count conflict, and direct routing.

lessons.title: Three evaluation methods, and a seven-day lookback
lessons.summary: All skills matching, best available skills, and disregard skills do different jobs. Proficiency covers ACD skills and language skills together.
paras: All skills matching selects the agent who has every required skill and the longest time since the last interaction. It does not use the skill rating. Best available skills considers the 100 agents with the longest time since the last interaction, keeps those who have every required skill, and assigns the interaction to the highest average proficiency. Equal averages go to the longest idle of that group. Disregard skills, next agent, selects the longest idle agent and does not consider skills.

The evaluation article says Genesys Cloud looks back 7 days when it chooses the next agent. An agent who has not been on queue for more than 7 days is not ranked by an older last-handled time. Proficiency scores are considered for ACD skills and language skills together. Status changes and on-queue behavior do not change that idle priority. If the agent belongs to several queues, idle time counts across those queues, not only the queue being evaluated.

figure.caption: All-skills sorts by idle time. Best-available sorts by proficiency inside a window of 100.

lessons.title: Bullseye widens the pool in two documented ways
lessons.summary: One way adds skill-expression groups. The other removes skills. The ring count is not the same sentence on every page.
paras: The bullseye overview describes expansion as concentric rings. Option 1 adds agents from groups on the next ring, and it tells you to use skill expression groups with the same skills at different proficiencies so WEM forecasting and scheduling can keep the planning group intact. Agents who lack the skills are not evaluated. Option 2 removes skills from the evaluation on the next ring. The skills stay on the interaction. Removal works best with all skills matching or best available skills. The settings article caps removals at 50 skills on one ring, and the delay is from 2 seconds to 259,200 seconds (72 hours).

The same settings article first says define up to five rings, then in the skill-removal steps says add rings up to six. Preferred-agent rings on that page also say up to six. The advanced routing overview says create up to six rings. The bullseye examples expand through ring 6. This lab will not pick a single cap those pages do not share. Count the rings the queue UI offers before you design a sixth. Inner-ring agents keep priority after an outer ring opens. Preferred agents are considered even without the required skills.
lessons.uncertainty: Opened in 2026-10: the settings article says define up to five rings and, later, up to six. The advanced routing overview says create up to six rings.

lessons.title: A skill expression filter replaces the queue’s skill list
lessons.summary: It works for standard and predictive routing when evaluation is All skills matching. Other methods ignore it.
paras: The evaluation article describes an optional ACD skill expression filter. You define a combination of skills and proficiencies in Architect, or supply it through the API, and Genesys Cloud applies it when the conversation transfers to a queue or while it waits. The filter is used instead of the ACD skills and language skills configured on the queue, and only when the routing method is standard or predictive and the evaluation method is All skills matching.

The same article says the filter does not work with preferred agent routing, last agent routing, direct routing, or bullseye routing. If no filter is defined, or the filter is invalid, routing uses the queue’s method and skill configuration. A filter is invalid when the expression has a syntax error, a skill or language skill cannot be resolved, or the expression cannot be evaluated at runtime.

figure.caption: A valid filter narrows the pool. An invalid filter falls back to the queue.

lessons.title: Direct routing still uses a queue
lessons.summary: The customer reaches a dedicated person. Wrap-up still exists, because the interaction is ACD.
paras: The direct routing overview says you route voice, SMS, and email to dedicated personnel, and the customer does not wait for the next available agent. The interaction is still ACD, still goes through a queue, and wrap-up codes are available. Direct routing is not supported for non-ACD interactions. The people who receive it must be On queue, or Off queue and Available with the Routing > Conversation – Accept Off-Queue permission.

If that person is unavailable, Genesys Cloud routes to a backup agent or queue. Backup queues and voicemail need an in-queue flow. A backup queue then uses its own routing method, and only On queue agents there receive it. A backup agent must be On queue, or Off queue and Available. Designating the direct number and the agent-level backup is done through APIs, as the overview states. The call path the article describes is: the number’s flow, a data action that finds the user, Transfer to ACD, then the in-queue flow if the agent does not answer.

lessons.title: Preferred scores are 0 to 100, and the list has a size
lessons.summary: Architect’s agent-score collection supports 20 pairs unless Customer Care raises it. More than 20 fails a call flow.
paras: The advanced routing overview says a preferred-agent score is the agent’s priority, from 0 to 100, and the highest score is the most preferred. Its example sets a case owner to 100 and backup agents to 90. If you do not have a preference, it says set the score to 100. In Architect, an agent-score collection supports up to 20 pairs. You can ask Customer Care to raise that maximum to 100. If a call flow supplies more than 20 pairs, the action takes the Failure path, and errorType is the string TooManyPreferredAgents. Email, chat, and message flows use their flow error handling instead.

The same overview says that for email, messaging, and inbound callbacks, preferred agent routing means Genesys Cloud no longer tries the last agent who handled the interaction. Scheduled callbacks are unaffected. Preferred-agent rings on the settings article expand up to six rings, with the same 2-second to 72-hour timing note used elsewhere on that page. Bullseye still considers preferred agents whether or not they have the required skills.

figure.caption: Higher score first. A list past 20 pairs fails the call flow.
